title: Antikythera Mechanism: The Oldest Computer on Record
description:
The oldest computer on record is a hand-cranked box of bronze gears, built by Greeks over 2,000 years ago. It tracked the Moon's uneven speed with a pin-and-slot gear and marked eclipses on a 223-month spiral dial.

Sources:
Antikythera mechanism, National Archaeological Museum, Athens (fragment inv. X 15087). Dated c. 150-100 BC / late 2nd century BC (dates are debated); found in the Antikythera shipwreck by sponge divers, recovered 1901.
Gears (about 30 survive), hand crank, Saros eclipse dial (223 months) and pin-and-slot lunar gearing: Deutsches Patent- und Markenamt, 'Antikythera-Mechanismus' (computer pioneers series); The New York Times (2006) on Freeth et al., Nature 444; Wikipedia, 'Antikythera mechanism'.
3D scene is a reconstruction, exploded view, not to scale.
